playstyle.role: The game's primary healer. A Doctor keeps a team alive with the two Complete Heals, a 38-step team-heal ladder, a 16-step team HP-buff ladder and heal-over-times, and contributes offensively through three simultaneous DoT lines and the unbreakable initiative debuff (UBT) that halves what a boss can do to the team.
playstyle.summary: The Doctor (profession 10) is the heal class. Its whole kit is verified in the local nano extraction: 240 castable nanos, of which 138 are heals or heal support (3 Complete Healing, 58 single-target heals, 38 team heals, 16 team HP buffs, 14 single HP buffs, 18 HoTs, 1 team HoT, 4 heal-delta buffs, 3 Treatment/First-Aid buffs, 2 cures) and 58 are DoTs across three simultaneous strains. It is the only profession that can cast Complete Healing (28650) and its team version Alpha and Omega (42409), and one of only two that can shut a mob's initiative off with an unbreakable debuff (Uncontrollable Body Tremors 99577). Play is: keep the team HP buff and Iron Circle up, keep a HoT rolling, land UBT on the mob, stack the three DoT lines, and spend the rest of the fight on the heal ladder. Weapon damage is a distant afterthought - Pistol is the only cheap weapon skill (cost factor 1.6) and it exists mainly to auto-attack while the DoTs tick.
strengths: Complete Healing (28650) and the team version Alpha and Omega (42409) - a fixed, un-modifiable full heal no other profession has. AOWiki: complete heals 'will always heal for 10001 health, ignoring heal modifying buffs'.

Depth of heal ladder: 58 single-target heals and 38 team heals in the local data, so there is a correctly-sized heal for every skill level from BM 29 (Weak Team Heal 42408) to BM 2153 (Superior Team Health Plan 273312).
Team HP buffs: a 16-step line from Enhance Team Health (42397, BM 18) to Superior Omni-Med Enhancement (95709, BM 852) that raises the whole team's max health and heals the amount raised.

Unbreakable initiative debuffs - Uncontrollable Body Tremors (99577) and Rapid Palsy (301845) 'last the full duration of the nano or until the target dies, regardless of damage dealt'. Tired Limbs (99578) scales to -2500 on all four initiatives.

Three DoT lines that stack simultaneously (DOT_LineA, DOT_LineB, DOTStrainC in the data - 58 DoTs), so a Doctor kills without ever needing a good weapon. Wrack and Ruin (28640) additionally strips 100 from every base attack skill.

Cheapest possible healing IP: Biological Metamorphosis, Matter Metamorphosis, Treatment, First Aid, Nano Pool, Nano C. Init, Computer Literacy, Tutoring and Pharma Tech are ALL cost factor 1.0 for a Doctor (skillcaps.json) - nine skills at the profession's best rate, more than any other class in the table.
Always wanted: a Doctor is the one team slot that is never optional, from Subway at level 10 to a 12-man Xan raid at 220.

Self-sufficient support kit: Iron Circle (42400, +20 Str/Sta), Instinctive Control (28669) / Improved (222856, +350 Nano C. Init), Nano Repulsor (28671) / Improved (222823, +200 Nano Resist), Superior First Aid (28675, +80 First Aid and Treatment), Epsilon Purge (28659) to strip DoT strains.
weaknesses: No burst damage. AOWiki: the Doctor 'must gradually wear down opponent defenses rather than burst damage'. Solo kills are DoT-timed, not damage-timed.

Weak weapon options. Pistol at cost 1.6 is the only cheap weapon; every other ranged skill a Doctor might use is 2.4 (Shotgun) or 4.0 (Rifle / Assault Rifle / Ranged Energy / Bow). AOWiki: 'Limited weapon skills can lead to a bumpy ride when going solo'.
Terrible close-combat evades: Evade-ClsC is cost 3.2, the Doctor's single worst defensive skill, and there is no evade or absorb nano in the kit at all.
The aggro magnet. Healing generates threat and a Doctor has no taunt-dump, no reflect and no absorb - it survives by max health, HP buffs on itself and the mob being initiative-debuffed.

Responsibility load. AOWiki: 'this profession is not for the faint-hearted' - team survival falls on the Doctor. The Funcom-forums teaming guide puts it as 'over 95% of all team deaths are due to a failure on the doc's part' (satirical, but that is how teams behave).

NCU pressure: keeping team HP buff + Iron Circle + Instinctive Control + Nano Repulsor + vaccines running, plus everyone else's offered buffs, fills NCU fast. The teaming guide's advice is that the Doctor is 'probably trying to keep 200 NCU free' - do not force buffs on one.
tips: Cast order in a team, before the pull: team HP buff (the 16-step line, best you can cast), Iron Circle (42400), then a HoT. The teaming guide: 'Make sure to ask for Iron Circle and the team HP buff before the rest of the team is in range.'

UBT first, damage second. Uncontrollable Body Tremors (99577, BM/PM 861) is unbreakable - land it on the mob and the whole fight becomes easier for the tank. Below that skill level use Rapid Palsy (301845, BM/PM 569), then Induce Muscle Spasms (99583, 389), Muscle Atrophy (99582, 93), Tired Limbs (99578, 29).
Complete Healing is not a big heal, it is a RESET. At BM 794 / MM 722 it becomes castable and from then on it is what saves a tank that took a spike - hold it, do not open with it.
Stack all three DoT strains. DOT_LineA, DOT_LineB and DOTStrainC are separate nanolines, so one nano from each runs at the same time. That, not the pistol, is a Doctor's damage.
Max Treatment every single level. It is cost 1.0 for a Doctor and it gates every implant and symbiant QL you will ever wear (Treatment req = trunc(4.7237*QL + 6.7673)).

Keep Matter Creation trained even on a pure healing build. It is what the short HP buffs (Life Channeler line) and the heal-delta buffs (Continuous Reconstruction 222824) require, not just the DoTs - Life Channeler (96247) needs BM 867 / MM 781 / MC 781.

Do not skip Time & Space. The 16-step TEAM HP buff line requires it (Superior Omni-Med Enhancement 95709 = BM 852 / MM 769 / SpaceTime 769). This is a local-data finding: the team HP buffs are the only Doctor line with a SpaceTime requirement.
Get an MP or a Trader on call. Composite Mochams (+140 to all six nano skills) and a Trader Wrangle are what let a Doctor cast the next heal tier and equip the next symbiant QL.
Level 218 and 220 are real power spikes: Cellular Rebirth (223297, level 218, heals 6001-7639) and Bodily Invigoration (223299, level 220, heals 7215-8385) both need Specialization 4 and Shadowlands.

Pick the weapon last. The whole weapon question for a Doctor is 'which item gives the most healing-relevant stats while holding a pistol' - see doctor-weapons.json; the Doctor-locked Pistol of Vitality / Vivacity / Endurance / Survival family and Doctor's Left Hand of Grace (267618, +5 HealMultiplier) exist for exactly that.

breed.reasoning: A Doctor's problem is not raw nano skill - its two healing schools (BM and MM) are already cost factor 1.0, the cheapest rate in the game - it is surviving the aggro that healing generates and meeting the Stamina/Psychic requirements its own gear carries. Solitus has no ability caps, the most forgiving IP spread, and enough HP/AC to stay standing; AO-Universe's Character Creation guide lists Solitus as a breed that 'tends to be a prefered breed among Adventurers, Doctors and Soldiers'. The gear side is concrete and read from the client data: Ofab Doctor QL300 needs Stamina 1099 and Psychic 854, and Chosen/Faithful Doctor QL300 needs Stamina 1099 and Psychic 899 - a Nanomage pays for that in ways Solitus does not.

alternatives.note: The pure-casting pick and also explicitly listed for Doctors: AO-Universe Character Creation says of Nanomage 'This breed is preferred among Metaphysicists, Nanotechnicians and Doctors', and it has the largest nano pool and best nano-cost percentages. The cost is HP and AC on a class that is already the fight's aggro magnet. Choose it for a buff-bot / raid-heal Doctor who will always be behind a tank.

The survivability pick ('troxdoc'). Most HP and best Body Dev, which directly answers the Doctor's real failure mode - dying to the aggro its own heals create. Pays for it with the lowest nano pool and worst Int/Psychic, so heals cost relatively more nano and the nano-skill requirements come later. Well-attested as a low-level twinking Doctor build (the Regidoc link thread catalogs 'Troxdoc with symbionts' setups).

Best evades and run speed. Tempting because the Doctor's evades are its weakest defensive stat, but Evade-ClsC is cost 3.2 for a Doctor no matter the breed, so the breed cannot fix that skill - Opifex is a niche PvP/kiting choice, not a healing optimum.

skillPriorities.why: Cost factor 1.0. The primary requirement on EVERY heal, HoT, HP buff and complete heal. AOWiki Doctor:Breed and Skills: 'Always max'. It is what decides which rung of the 58-step single-heal and 38-step team-heal ladders you can stand on (Weak Team Heal 42408 at BM 29 -> Superior Team Health Plan 273312 at BM 2153).
Cost factor 1.0. The second requirement on every heal and every HP buff, tracking BM at roughly 90% of its value. AOWiki: 'Always max'. Improved Complete Healing (270747) needs BM 2153 AND MM 2153.

Cost factor 1.0 - tied for the Doctor's cheapest skill. Gates every implant and symbiant QL (Treatment = trunc(4.7237*QL + 6.7673), so a QL200 implant needs ~947) and every heal/nano kit. AOWiki: 'Always max'.

Cost factor 1.6. The other half of the initiative-debuff line - Uncontrollable Body Tremors (99577) needs BM 861 AND PM 861. AOWiki is explicit: 'Always max, even after you can cast UBT'. Also gates Superior First Aid (28675, PM 571) and Improved Instinctive Control (222856, PM 1033).
Cost factor 1.0. AOWiki: 'Always Max'. A Doctor chain-casts for an entire fight; the nano bar is the fight timer.
Cost factor 2.0. AOWiki: 'Always Max'. The Doctor has no reflect, no absorb and bad evades - raw HP is the only mitigation it owns, and healing pulls aggro.
Cost factor 1.0. AOWiki: 'always max' Nano Initiative. Cast and recharge speed on the heal ladder IS the Doctor's throughput; a faster Complete Healing is worth more than any weapon upgrade.

Cost factor 1.0. AOWiki: 'always max'. NCU is the Doctor's binding constraint - team HP buff, Iron Circle, Instinctive Control, Nano Repulsor, vaccines and everyone else's offered buffs all compete for it.

Cost factor 1.6. Required by the short/single HP buffs (Life Channeler 96247 = MC 781), the heal-delta buffs (Continuous Reconstruction 222824 = MC 619), Malpractice (275701 = MC 1727) and the entire DoT kit. AOWiki Doctor Nano Programs: 'Even a Doctor that wants only healing and buffs cannot forego Matter Creation'.

Cost factor 1.6. Read from the local data: the 16 TEAM HP buffs are the only Doctor line carrying a SpaceTime requirement - Superior Omni-Med Enhancement (95709) needs SpaceTime 769, and the top team HoT Team-Enhanced Deathless Blessing (269455) needs 810. Also gates Epsilon Purge (28659, SpaceTime 696) and Nano Repulsor.
Cost factor 1.6. Gates the utility half of the kit: Epsilon Purge (28659, SI 696), Superior First Aid (28675, SI 517), Instinctive Control (28669, SI 388) and Improved (222856, SI 1033).
Cost factor 1.0. Stims are the Doctor's instant self-heal while a cast is on cooldown, and First Aid gates their QL. Superior First Aid (28675) buffs it +80 for everyone including yourself.

Cost factor 1.6 - the ONLY cheap weapon skill a Doctor has (Shotgun 2.4, MG/SMG 3.2, Rifle / Assault Rifle / Ranged Energy / Bow all 4.0). 17 of the 23 Doctor-locked weapons in items.ocp are pistols. Train it to wield the item you want, not for its damage.

Cost factor 2.4 - the cheapest pistol special for a Doctor (Burst 3.0, Aimed Shot 3.2, Full Auto 4.0) and the one present on almost every pistol in the data. Only worth IP if you actually auto-attack.
Cost factor 1.2 - unusually cheap for a Doctor, and it is what stops a Trader draining you or a mob landing its debuff mid-heal. Self-buffable with Improved Nano Repulsor (222823, +200).

Cost factor 3.2. Only if you actually auto-attack with a pistol. AOWiki: raise Melee or Ranged Initiative 'when you can, or until you're hitting 1/1' depending on your weapon choice - for a Doctor that is usually never, because Nano C. Init matters more.
Cost factor 2.0 - cheaper than Ranged Init (3.2) and Melee Init (3.2). Relevant only if you run Martial Arts (cost 2.0, the Doctor's other cheap weapon option).
Cost factor 2.4 each - the Doctor's two affordable evades. Evade-ClsC is 3.2 and is the skill to give up on; nothing in the Doctor's own kit buffs evades.

Cost factor 1.0. AO-Universe: 'Doctors have a particular tradeskill they are good with, specifically PhamaTech.' Used for stims/health-kit building and buffed by the Alchemist perk line (+200 Chemistry and Pharma Tech at 6 tiers).
Cost factor 2.3. The reason to train it at endgame is Alien/Combined armor assembly, which is Psychology-gated; otherwise it is the least-useless Ear-bright implant cluster.

skillPriorities.skill: Electrical Engineering / Quantum FT / Nano Programming
skillPriorities.why: All cost factor 1.6 - cheap for a Doctor. Nano Programming lets you build your own implant clusters; EE/QFT feed the implant and armor tradeskill chains.
Cost factor 1.5 - oddly cheap for a Doctor and the only reason the Right Hand shiny implant slot is not pure filler.
Cost factor 2.4. Positioning to stay in heal range without standing in the melee. Ofab/Chosen Doctor boots carry +RunSpeed (Penultimate Ofab Doctor Boots 264671 = +55 at QL300).

skillPriorities.skill: Melee/Ranged weapon skills other than Pistol and Martial Arts
skillPriorities.why: Rifle, Assault Rifle, Ranged Energy, Bow, Multi Ranged, Heavy Weapons, Full Auto and Aimed Shot are all cost factor 4.0 for a Doctor - the most expensive tier in the table. Do not spend IP there.

research.name: Bedside Manner
research.effect: 10 levels. Pistol-skill focused; grants the proc perks Healing Care and Antiseptic.

research.name: Internship
research.effect: 10 levels. Increases NCU and Pharma Tech; grants the proc perks Blood Transfusion, Pathogen and Massive Vitae Plan.
research.note: NCU is the Doctor's binding constraint (team HP buff + Iron Circle + Instinctive Control + Nano Repulsor + vaccines), so this line is worth more to a Doctor than its name suggests. Three procs from one line.

research.name: Rehabilitation
research.effect: 10 levels. Develops the metamorphosis skills (BM/MM); grants the proc perks Inflammation and Astringent.
research.note: Direct BM/MM progression = directly higher heals. High priority.

research.name: Diagnosis
research.effect: 10 levels. Boosts health and stamina; grants the proc perk Anesthetic.
research.note: HP and Stamina - the Doctor's survivability and the Stamina its own Ofab/Chosen armor requires (1099 at QL300).

research.name: Toxicology
research.effect: 10 levels. Enhances Matter Creation and nano capacity; grants the proc perks Anatomic Blight and Dangerous Culture.

research.name: Underground Doctor
research.effect: 10 levels (perk items 261166-261175). Grants the proc perk Restrictive Bandaging and a 5% healing efficiency bonus.
research.note: A flat 5% on all healing at the end of the line. The client data backs the healing claim - the Underground Doctor perk item 261175 carries a HealMultiplier bonus of +5.

research.name: Aggressive Surgery
research.effect: 10 levels. Enhances ranged combat abilities; grants a proc perk (see the Muscle Memory / Muscular Malaise note in perks).
research.note: The offensive/ranged line - lowest priority for a healing Doctor unless you actually shoot things.

research.name: Global Research (all-profession)
research.effect: Shared cross-profession global research lines; applies to a Doctor exactly as to any other profession.
research.note: Not Doctor-specific; standard global picks apply. Research needs Lost Eden - a froob Doctor has none of this.

_deviations: Breed recommendation is Solitus, not the MP file's Nanomage. The MP is recommended Nanomage because its power scales with nano SKILL, and Nanomage's Int/Psychic is what buys nano skill. A Doctor's two healing schools are already cost factor 1.0 (vs 1.0 for the MP's MC/TS too), so the marginal nano skill buys less, while the Doctor is the fight's aggro magnet and its own armor (Ofab/Chosen Doctor QL300: Stamina 1099, Psychic 854-899) is Stamina-gated. Nanomage is kept as the first alternative and is explicitly named for Doctors by AO-Universe; Atrox is a real, attested Doctor build ('troxdoc') in a way it is not for an MP.

There is no 'pet' dimension at all. The MP build file is organised around which pets you can keep up; the Doctor build is organised around which rung of the heal ladder you can stand on, which is why the skill priorities quote nano-skill NUMBERS from castReqs (BM 29 -> 2153) rather than pet tiers.

Nine skills at cost factor 1.0. The MP has five (Nano Pool, MM, BM, Nano C. Init, Matter Creation, Time & Space, Nano Programming, Tutoring, Computer Literacy - nine as well, but distributed differently); the Doctor's 1.0 set is BM, MM, Treatment, First Aid, Nano Pool, Nano C. Init, Computer Literacy, Tutoring, Pharma Tech. The practical difference is that TREATMENT and FIRST AID are 1.0 for a Doctor and 2.0 for an MP, which is why 'max Treatment every level' is a hard rule here and only a ladder note in the MP file.

Weapon skills are cheaper and matter slightly more than for an MP. Pistol is 1.6 for a Doctor (2.4 for an MP) and Martial Arts 2.0 (2.8), and 23 weapon models in items.ocp carry a Profession EqualTo Doctor lock, 17 of them pistols. The MP file says 'weapon skills are expensive and secondary'; for a Doctor Pistol is a real, cheap, supported choice - it is still not a damage plan.

The Doctor has AI/alien perk lines worth maxing (Champion of Nano Combat +100 to all six nano skills, Embrace +1000 Max Nano). The MP file's alien perk entry is 'Ancient Knowledge - bugged, avoid'. This is a genuine class difference, not a difference in how the file was written.

Research-line-to-proc mapping is FULLY sourced here (wiki.aodb.us Doctor:Research_Lines names the procs per line and every name is confirmed as an item/nano in itemnames.sql). The MP file had to mark the Sow Doubt / Sow Despair / Thoughtful Means mapping as inferred; that gap does not exist for the Doctor.

Evades are treated as a lost cause rather than a priority. The MP file lists 'Dodge Ranged / Evade Close Combat / Duck Explosives - keep high or max whenever possible' (MP evades are 1.6/1.6/2.4). A Doctor pays 2.4/2.4/3.2 and has no evade nano, so the advice here is Body Dev. and HP buffs instead.
_unverified: Which of 'Muscle Memory' (PerkHash LEProcDoctorMuscleMemory; itemnames 263491/263514/267034) and 'Muscular Malaise' (itemnames 266812, named by wiki.aodb.us as the Aggressive Surgery proc) is the PERK and which is the nano it fires. Both names exist in the client data; the relationship was not resolved.

Per-tier values for every perk line: the numbers quoted (e.g. Assault Force Medic +340 Max Health / +43 BM / +43 MM / +40 Treatment / +25 First Aid) are the MAX-rank totals as stated by wiki.aodb.us Doctor:Perks. Per-tier breakdowns and the level at which each tier unlocks were NOT read from the client data and are not given here.

The recommendedAtLevel field is priority guidance, not a sourced unlock level - unlike the MP file, no per-perk level table was located for the Doctor. Treat every recommendedAtLevel as 'when you can', not as a gate.

The Solitus-over-Nanomage recommendation is a judgement built on (a) AO-Universe naming Solitus as preferred for Doctors, (b) AO-Universe ALSO naming Nanomage as preferred for Doctors, and (c) the Stamina/Psychic requirements read from the Doctor's own armor in items.ocp. No single source states 'Solitus is the best Doctor breed'. wiki.aodb.us Doctor:Breed_and_Skills does NOT name a recommended breed at all.

Specialist Healer's '+21% healing' is the wiki's number; what the client data independently confirms is only that the ten Specialist Healer perk items carry HealMultiplier +2/+3. The unit and stacking of HealMultiplier were not derived.

'Over 95% of all team deaths are due to a failure on the doc's part' is quoted from a deliberately satirical Funcom-forums teaming guide. It is recorded as a description of team EXPECTATIONS, not as a mechanic.

Skill cost factors are quoted exactly from reference/skillcaps.json (column index 3 = 'Doctor' in _professionOrder). That file's own _dependencyReliability caveats apply; the cost numbers themselves are used verbatim, never rounded or estimated.
